newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed amid steady dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed amid steady dlr.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Monday with steady trade in the Canadian dollar providing support for the market, analysts said.

"The currency is remaining relatively firm this morning," said Barry Davenport, a senior vice-president of treasury with Bank of Montreal. "What's probably influencing the market (most) is a bit of an adjustment as a result of the very strong performance of the fixed-income markets last week."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.01 percent from 3.03 percent at Friday's close.
Canada's dollar was little changed from Friday's close in early morning trade on Monday after firming overnight in Asia.

"The dollar is a touch weaker but nothing significant. Most people are just going to rest on their laurels a little while," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "It (the morning) just feels like it doesn't want to go anywhere."
Dealers said Canadian economic reports out this morning on foreign reserves and building permits had little to no impact on the money market.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.37 percent from 3.42 percent at Friday's close. The one-year T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.97 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
